informative.title: Snap detections to local maxima
informative.summary: Refines detection sample positions by moving each detection to the maximum signal sample in a NaN-aware local search window.
informative.description: This tool defines local-maximum snapping used by ECG detection pipelines to refine approximate detections onto nearby R-wave maxima while treating NaN ECG samples as signal gaps.
notes: Implementations use native sample coordinates: one-based in MATLAB, zero-based in Python. Shared conformance fixtures use one-based coordinates; normalize input and output positions at the test boundary.
NaN values are accepted in ecg as hard signal-gap boundaries and in detections as missing detection markers.
Inf and -Inf values in ecg or detections are invalid.

definitions.text: For an ECG of length N, finite detections must lie in [1, N] in MATLAB and [0, N-1] in Python, before rounding. Round valid detections to the nearest integer with exact half-way values rounded toward the larger index. Shared cases express both input and output coordinates as one-based positions. Subtract one when calling Python and add one to its finite results before conformance comparison.
window_size is rounded to the nearest integer number of samples before constructing search windows; exact positive half-way values round upward. A positive radius below 0.5 rounds to zero.

A finite ECG segment is a maximal contiguous run of ecg samples that are neither NaN nor infinite. NaN samples are hard boundaries between finite ECG segments; Inf and -Inf samples are invalid inputs.

For each rounded valid detection d on a finite ECG sample, search from max(first_position, segment_start, d - effective_window_size) through min(last_position, segment_end, d + effective_window_size), inclusive. first_position and last_position use the implementation index origin, as do the finite segment boundaries.

The refined detection is the native sample position of the first maximum-valued ECG sample inside the clipped finite search_window for that detection. If the corresponding detection is NaN, or if its rounded position falls on a NaN ECG sample, the refined detection is NaN.

behavior.nan_handling: NaN values in ecg are allowed and act as hard segment boundaries. Snapping for a finite valid detection must search only inside the contiguous finite ECG segment containing that detection and must not omit NaNs in a way that crosses gaps. NaN values in detections are allowed missing detection markers and produce NaN in the corresponding refined_detections element. If a finite detection falls on a NaN ECG sample, the corresponding refined_detections element is NaN. Inf and -Inf values in either ecg or detections are invalid.
behavior.empty_input: Empty ecg input is invalid. Empty detections input returns an empty refined_detections vector.
behavior.input_orientation: Row and column vectors represent the same canonical ecg and detections sequences. refined_detections is a one-dimensional ordered vector aligned with detections.
behavior.insufficient_data: Validate finite detection bounds before rounding: MATLAB positions less than 1 or greater than length(ecg), or Python positions less than 0 or greater than length(ecg)-1, are invalid. Search windows near signal boundaries or NaN ECG gaps are clipped to valid finite ECG sample positions.
